video_title: The Second Apron Complaints Are Getting Louder | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: David Kelly's criticism of the NBA's second apron rules
quotes.excerpt: the second apron is obviously in the news because of some of the changes Boston had to make
quotes.quote: The second apron is obviously in the news because of some of the changes Boston had to make. Now you have David Kelly, who is the executive director of the NBA Players Association, coming out and saying that the second apron basically sucks, that it should not have been that the union should not have allowed it to go into place a few years ago. And that when the next round of negotiations comes up, that is going to be something that they fight against.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the second apron on player salaries and movement
quotes.excerpt: installing what is essentially a hard cap in a league that didn't have one is bad for players

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I think the Players Association is absolutely right. Installing what is essentially a hard cap in a league that didn't have one is bad for the players. We used to have more free spending, now we have less of it. You know who that affects most? The players. Also, it affects the fans because it affects teams staying together or not. Homegrown stars like Jaylen Brown, do they end up leaving?

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The second apron is working exactly how it should be working.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The second apron's role in preventing teams from overspending
quotes.excerpt: it is a hard cap on salaries that keeps them from working against themselves by being so competitive
quotes.quote: Adam Silver's bosses absolutely think that the second apron is a great idea because it is a hard cap on salaries that keeps them from working against themselves by being so competitive that they outspend each other. That is why that was put in. In the next collective bargaining agreement, are the players going to get any relief on this? No, because the players have no power in collective bargaining agreements.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's perspective on his contract and team security
quotes.excerpt: Brunson says that he took the most money he possibly could because he wanted the security
quotes.quote: Brunson says that he took the most money he possibly could because he wanted the security. I think in his mind, he still looked at himself back then as being somewhat disposable, that if he didn't continue this trajectory, that the Knicks, even with Leon Rose there, that they would maybe discard him, trade him, do something else. So he wanted the max dollar he could possibly get in that moment.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The need for no-trade clauses in the current CBA environment
quotes.excerpt: you better bring no-trade clauses back because that is what I would ask for

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: They are, but then you better bring no-trade clauses back because that is what I would ask for. We keep talking about how someone is the last person to have one. Bradley Beal got one.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I think it is because you get to spend a certain amount of years with one team, like 10 and 5.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Advocating for exceptions for homegrown talent in the salary cap
quotes.excerpt: there should be exceptions carved in for homegrown talent
quotes.quote: There should be exceptions carved in for homegrown talent. I think what happened in Boston should not be forced to happen again. Now, Boston is maybe a little bit different. There is a lot going on behind the scenes with Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum, and the Celtics that contributed to this divorce, but fundamentally, it is hard to build a team when you have two players making up 70% of your salary cap.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of dynasties on the health of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: everyone knows who Stephen Curry is because of how many times he won the title
quotes.quote: I think there is a lot of things that go into whether we have dynasties or not. Everyone knows who Stephen Curry is because of how many times he won the title and that is good for the NBA. Dynasties made Michael Jordan famous and Michael Jordan being famous helped the entire NBA. So dynasties aren't bad for the NBA, just as a matter of course, but I do think it is great to have these eras where more fans get to experience winning.
